title: Probability Distributions and Elementary Limit Theorems
description: Probability spaces and axioms; conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem; random variables, distribution functions and expectation; moment and probability generating functions; the standard discrete and continuous distributions; joint distributions, independence and change of variable; and Markov's and Chebyshev's inequalities, modes of convergence and the limit theorems. The folder has no lecture notes, so the course follows the outline in a student's notes, with those notes used where they apply and the rest written from general knowledge.

topics.title: Probability Spaces and Axioms
topics.summary: Probability measures how likely events are, defined by the classical, empirical and axiomatic approaches. A probability measure on a sample space satisfies Kolmogorov's axioms, from which the complement, addition and inclusion-exclusion rules follow.
subtopics: Random experiments, sample spaces and events
Counting: sampling with and without replacement

topics.title: Conditional Probability, Independence and Bayes' Theorem
topics.summary: Conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B) updates a probability given that B occurred. Events are independent when P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B); the law of total probability and Bayes' theorem reverse the conditioning over a partition.
subtopics: Independent events; pairwise and mutual independence
Partitions and the law of total probability
Applications: medical tests, references, rental cars

topics.title: Random Variables, Distribution Functions and Expectation
topics.summary: A random variable assigns a number to each outcome; it is discrete with a probability mass function or continuous with a density. The distribution function F(x) = P(X ≤ x) gives probabilities of intervals, and expectation and variance summarise the distribution.
subtopics: The cumulative distribution function and its properties

topics.title: Moment and Probability Generating Functions
topics.summary: The moment generating function M(t) = E(e^(tX)) produces the moments of X by differentiation at t = 0. The probability generating function G(s) = E(s^X) does the same for discrete variables, and both uniquely identify a distribution.
subtopics: Moments about the origin and the mean
Finding mean and variance from the MGF
MGF of a sum of independent variables

topics.title: Standard Discrete and Continuous Distributions
topics.summary: Important discrete distributions are the Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson and discrete uniform; important continuous ones are the uniform, exponential, gamma and normal. Each has a known probability function, moment generating function, mean and variance.
subtopics: Table of MGFs, means and variances

topics.title: Joint Distributions, Independence and Transformations
topics.summary: Two random variables have a joint pdf or pmf, from which marginal and conditional distributions follow. They are stochastically independent when the joint density factorises; sums of independent variables and change of variable give the distributions of new variables.
subtopics: Joint probability density and mass functions
Distribution of sums of independent random variables

topics.title: Inequalities, Convergence and Limit Theorems
topics.summary: Markov's and Chebyshev's inequalities bound tail probabilities using only the mean and variance. Sequences of random variables converge in probability, in distribution, in mean square or almost surely, giving the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.
subtopics: The weak law of large numbers
